classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the last two digits determine each remainder because every modulus divides 100.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is $52\,348\,181$ modulo $4$? Is there an easier way than dividing?

answer.worked:
Every multiple of $100$ is divisible by $4$, so only the last two digits affect the remainder.

$$\begin{align*}81&=4\times20+1\\52\,348\,181&\equiv1\pmod4\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is $52\,348\,181$ modulo $100$? Is there an easier way than dividing?

answer.worked:
The last two digits give the remainder after division by $100$.

$$\begin{align*}52\,348\,181&=100\times523\,481+81\\52\,348\,181&\equiv81\pmod{100}\end{align*}$$
